And in the year 1027 [715-716 AD],
that Maslama entered the country of Asia,
and conquered Pergamon and Rhodes,
and carried them off into captivity.
And in that same year, Sulayman prepared Maslama to go against Constantinople.
And he gathered two hundred thousand troops,
and five thousand ships full of troops and provisions.
And he gathered twelve thousand pioneers {qūlāgārē},
(i.e., qalāgārē,
laborers?), and six thousand camels and six thousand donkeys that were carrying provisions, weapons, and components of siege-engines {mangonels}.
And he made 'Umar ibn Hubayra another commander over them.
Moreover, thirty thousand additional warriors went in with them, those who went out to fight at their own expense and from their own means,
that is to say, 'in the way of God',
and in their language they are called Mutatawwi'a.
And two armies marched for the Arabs:
one by sea and the other by land.
Now Leo, the commander of the Romans, when he met Maslama, the commander of the Arabs,
promised to help them to conquer the royal city,
and they promised him the kingdom of the Romans.
Now Emperor Theodosius, when he perceived Leo's treachery,
seized his family and imprisoned them in the city of Amorium.
And when Leo heard [this], he went to King Sulayman,
because he too had advanced with twelve thousand men against the city of Chalcedon,
in order to cut off the provisions that were entering Constantinople.
And he took six thousand troops
and struck against Amorium.
And when the people of the city were afraid,
they gave him his family.
And he dismissed the Arabs,
giving each man twelve dinars.
And he and the Romans set out straight toward Constantinople.
And when he met the forces of the Romans,
he showed them that he was dealing with the Arabs with guile;
and they were pleased with him,
and made him king over them.
And when he reached Constantinople,
Theodosius went out, was tonsured, and became a cleric.
And Leo reigned twenty-four years.
And with vain hope he began to hold off the Arabs, while strengthening the city with provisions and otherwise.
And when Maslama learned that Leo had deceived him,
he swiftly crossed the strait of the sea,
and encamped against Constantinople.
